Catalan

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin supplēre, with normal change of conjugation to -ir.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic) [suˈpli]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [suˈpliɾ]

Verb

[edit]

suplir (first-person singular present supleixo, first-person singular preterite suplí, past participle suplert or suplit)

  1. (transitive) to substitute
  2. (transitive) to replace

Indonesian

[edit]
Indonesian Wikipedia has an article on:
suplir
Wikipedia id

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Dutch chevelure, from French chevelure.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈsup.lir/

Noun

[edit]

suplir (plural suplir-suplir)

  1. (biology) maidenhair fern

Further reading

[edit]
  • “suplir”, in Kamus Besar Bahasa Indonesia [Great Dictionary of the Indonesian Language] (in Indonesian), Jakarta: Agency for Language Development and Cultivation – Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology of the Republic of Indonesia, 2016

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin supplēre.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /suˈpliɾ/ [suˈpliɾ]
  • Rhymes: -iɾ
  • Syllabification: su‧plir

Verb

[edit]

suplir (first-person singular present suplo, first-person singular preterite suplí, past participle suplido)

  1. to substitute
    Synonym: sustituir
  2. to supply
    Synonyms: abastecer, proveer, suministrar
  3. to eke out
    Synonym: complimentar
